excerpt: Statespace (State Space Labs) is the New York company behind Aimlabs, the free aim trainer for first-person shooter players. Aimlabs+ costs from $7 a month.
content:
Statespace, legally State Space Labs, Inc., is a New York company that makes Aimlabs (earlier written Aim Lab), a training app for players of first-person shooter games. Players run short exercises that test and train aiming skills such as flicking, tracking and reaction time, and Aimlabs measures each shot to show where they are improving. The website says Aimlabs has more than 40 million players, over 50,000 tasks and playlists, an AI-powered coach and profiles for 500 FPS games, and that it is an official partner of Valorant and Rainbow Six Siege. In 2026 it released Aimlabs 2.0. The old statespace.gg domain no longer resolves; the company now operates under the Aimlabs name.

GamesBeat reported that founder and CEO Wayne Mackey was a postdoctoral fellow in the Computational Neuroimaging Lab at New York University, and that the company draws on neuroscience for its training methods.

Funding

Statespace raised a $15 million Series A in 2020 led by Khosla Ventures, according to Esports Insider. TechCrunch reported a $29 million Series B in November 2020, when Aim Lab had passed 1.5 million monthly active users. In September 2021 it raised a $50 million Series C co-led by Khosla Ventures and Lux Capital, taking total funding past $98 million; GamesBeat said Aim Lab then had 5 million monthly active users and 20 million total players. Weeks later it acquired ProGuides, an esports coaching platform.

Pricing

Aimlabs is free to play. Its paid membership, Aimlabs+, costs $10 a month on a monthly plan, $9 a month billed every three months, or $7 a month billed every six months, and adds a sensitivity finder, guided training programmes, an AI aim coach, advanced metrics and a 50% discount in the Aimlabs shop.

We have not tested Aimlabs. This page is based on the Aimlabs website and membership page (checked 15 October 2026) and on GamesBeat, TechCrunch and Esports Insider.
